title: Allocator fanout spike and autoscale oscillation retro (scratch)
content:
Summary:

This is a working retro and ops-scribble for the 2026-02-17/18 GPU pool degradation that manifested as sudden latency spikes and an autoscaler oscillation loop in the dedicated-gpu-westus pool. Primary observable: a rapid allocator fanout that caused many small scheduling attempts, KV-cache amplification, and short-lived evictions which triggered autoscaler scale-up/scale-down thrash.

High-level impact:
- Time window: ~2026-02-17 22:40 -> 2026-02-18 01:05 UTC (approx).
- Affected pool: dedicated-gpu-westus (pool-id: gw-us-ded-12).
- Symptom: 95th token latency increased from ~120ms to 950ms; request failure rate (5xx) spiked from 0.2% -> 3.6%.
- Business: a handful of mid-size customers saw degraded throughput and timed-out batches, some failing canary routes.

Timeline (rough):
- 22:36 UTC: first latency anomaly detected by synthetic runs (per-route 95p) — alert P3 to oncall.
- 22:40 UTC: oncall saw allocator scheduling error rate tick up; multiple small unschedulable messages.
- 22:44 UTC: autoscaler triggered scale-up (added 4 nodes) based on short-window CPU/GPU slot pressure.
- 22:48 UTC: after new nodes came up, scheduler attempted high-concurrency placement which caused excessive KV cache writes and eviction churn.
- 22:50-23:15 UTC: repeated scale-downs/scale-ups (oscillation) as short-lived pressure windows bounced past thresholds.
- 23:20 UTC: SRE manual mitigation: applied temporary limiter to scheduler fanout and increased autoscaler cool-down to 10m.
- 23:40 UTC: latency returned to baseline; gradual recovery and postmortem triage started.

Initial detection signals and useful queries:
- PromQL: sum(rate(allocator_attempts_total[1m])) by (pool) — sharp spike visible for gw-us-ded-12.
- PromQL: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le, route)) — shows token latency.
- Logs: scheduler WARN logs showing "placement retry due to transient topology mismatch" repeated with different tenant IDs.
- Grafana: KV cache write amplification metric increased ~6x concurrent writes vs normal.

Investigation notes and hypotheses tested:
1) Noisy tenant causing eviction cascade
- Evidence: a small set of tenant IDs had repeated large-batch jobs queued during window; their request patterns aligned with first spike.
- Counter-evidence: eviction traces show the scheduler attempted placement across *many* nodes at once, not a single-tenant hot-shot.
- Conclusion: noisy tenant amplified the problem but not sole root cause.

2) Allocator fanout bug combined with topology changes
- Evidence: allocator logs show a new codepath (recent runtime PR merged 2026-02-10) that increases candidate node fanout for placement when free-slot fragmentation detected.
- We reproduced in sim harness: under fragmented slot distribution + short-lived node additions, the allocator will probe many nodes concurrently causing lock contention and repeated writes to the KV cache.
- Conclusion: allocator fanout is primary trigger.

3) Autoscaler hysteresis too aggressive/too short window
- Evidence: autoscaler decided to scale up quickly on transient signals (1m window) and then scaled down after 3m, making oscillation likely.
- Conclusion: autoscaler config (scaleDownStabilizationPeriod) too low for this workload pattern.

Root cause (synthesized):
- A recent allocator change (PR #1887) increases node candidate fanout in fragmentation scenarios. During a transient surge of a few noisy tenants, the allocator probed too many nodes concurrently, causing KV cache write amplification and lock contention. That increased token latencies and triggered the autoscaler to react to transient pressure. Autoscaler configured with short cool-down windows caused scale-up/scale-down oscillation which worsened fragmentation, creating a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Applied a temporary scheduler rate limiter (rollout flag: scheduler.maxPlacementConcurrency=16) as a kill-switch (2026-02-17 23:20 UTC).
- Increased autoscaler scaleDownStabilizationPeriod from 180s -> 600s for gw-us-ded pools.
- Blackholed the top-3 noisy tenant IDs from multi-tenant packing (moved them to reserved nodes) for 2 hours.
- Throttled large-batch job queueing (rate limit per-tenant workers) for affected customers.

Recovery validation steps executed:
- Synthetic canaries returned to baseline; 95p token latency checked every 1m for 30m post-change.
- No further allocator_attempt spikes seen in 60m after limiter.

Runbook gaps discovered (candidate edits):
- Add explicit circuit-breaker for allocator fanout: limit concurrent node probes per placement to X and expose as feature flag.
- Autoscaler guidance: document recommended stabilization windows per pool size and workload class (heavy-batch vs steady-llm).
- Add an observability dashboard that correlates allocator_attempts, KV-cache-write-rate, autoscaler-events, and pool-fragmentation-index.
- Escalation path: add checklist to move noisy tenants to dedicated-reserved pools (automated script currently manual).

Action items (owners and tentative ETA):
- SRE/Serving-runtime (Aisha): revert or throttle the new fanout codepath behind config flag and run full sim (ETA: 2026-02-28).
- Runtime eng (Lena): add per-placement concurrency limiter + tests + feature flag (ETA: 2026-03-05).
- Autoscaler (Tom): bump default scaleDownStabilizationPeriod to 600s for dedicated pools and add safety hysteresis; add canary config (ETA: 2026-02-26).
- Observability (Marco): create combined allocator/kv/autoscaler dashboard and alert rule (ETA: 2026-03-03).
- Oncall tooling (SRE): script to move noisy tenants to reserved nodes and rollback instructions (ETA: 2026-03-01).

Follow-up experiments to run:
- Synthetic sim: reproduce fragmentation + node-add/remove + noisy-tenant pattern with current allocator vs throttled allocator; measure median and 95p latencies and KV write amplification.
- Autoscaler stress test: run synthetic short bursts to find best stabilization windows for pools of size 8/16/32.
- KV cache contention profiling: attach pprof during sim to confirm hotspots are lock/serialize points in cache writes.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Was there any secondary contributor from underlying infra (cloud host churn)? Initial checks show no host-level firmware or driver alerts, but need deeper infra audit.
- How many customers were actually affected downstream (CS followup needed).
- Should we move to per-tenant packing limits by default for all dedicated pools? Operational cost vs benefit to evaluate.

Notes for postmortem writeup (what to include):
- Short summary and timeline (what happened in plain English).
- Root cause analysis with evidence and minimal reproducible sim.
- List of mitigations taken during incident, and permanent fixes planned.
- Runbook changes and new dashboards/alerts.
- Customer impact summary (to be filled after CS data).

Quick commands & playbook snippets (for oncall):
- Temporarily limit placement concurrency:
  kubectl patch config scheduler --patch '{"spec":{"maxPlacementConcurrency":16}}'
- Increase autoscaler cool-down for pool (one-off):
  curl -XPOST $CONTROL_PLANE/api/pools/gw-us-ded-12/autoscaler/config -d '{"scaleDownStabilizationPeriod":600}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Move tenant to reserved pool (manual):
  ./scripts/move-tenant.sh --tenant-id T-12345 --from gw-us-ded-12 --to reserved-gw-us-1

References and links:
- Linear SRE-3421 (incident tracking): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/SRE-3421
- Confluence sim notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/allocator-fanout-sim
- Runtime PR with fanout change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/1887
- Slack thread: #sre-dedicated (thread ts: 1676730...)

Appendix: quick metrics snapshot during peak (derived from Grafana)
- allocator_attempts_total rate (1m): baseline ~120/s -> peak ~1.2k/s
- KV_cache_write_rate (writes/s): baseline ~800/s -> peak ~5.1k/s
- pool_free_slot_fragmentation_index: baseline 0.22 -> peak 0.64 (scale 0-1)
- autoscaler scale events: 3x scale-up / 4x scale-down during window

Notes-to-self: preserve sim harness run logs, mark PR 1887 for close review, follow up with runtime team retro.
